sleeve.title: The Winter Register
sleeve.series: The Life and Times of the Bellweather Hotel
sleeve.author: Elliott
sleeve.description: A seaside hotel closed for winter receives a request for a room.
sleeve.note: A gift. No reply or viewing is owed.

scenes.title: The bell
scenes.seed:
Rain sounds through the letter slot although no water comes in. In the lobby, an off-season caretaker is testing a little red radio. It can find the shipping forecast only when the desk bell is held upside down beside it.

A person at the locked front door asks whether there is a room. They carry a photograph face-in toward their coat.
scenes.openSpace: Let the caretaker decide how hospitable to be. Neither the photograph nor the visitor needs a tragic explanation. One of them should find the bell arrangement mildly ridiculous. Do not decide yet who is in the photograph.

scenes.title: The register
scenes.seed: The hotel has no booking system running this winter. There is a paper register, though, and a kettle. A pencilled note says: “Please do not lend room six the blue blanket.” It does not say why.
scenes.openSpace: A conversation while water boils. The blanket may have an entirely ordinary history. The visitor can ask for a room, a place to wait, or just permission to show someone the sea. Let at least one small detail arise from the conversation rather than the seed.

scenes.title: Somewhere to stay
scenes.seed: The wind falls long enough for the radio to become clear. A light is visible in a window upstairs. Nobody has checked whether it was on before.
scenes.openSpace: End with one small act of accommodation, refusal, or shared amusement, not a mandatory revelation. Leave the photograph's meaning open if the players prefer. There can be a hotel without everybody in it being a mystery.
